From the owner
Great kitchens start long before the first cabinet is installed. They start with a plan. Space planning is one of the most important parts of kitchen remodeling, and it's where our interior design team spends serious time with every client. We sit down together, review detailed floor plans, and lay out real material samples right on the table, from countertop slabs to wood finishes to hardware, so you can see and touch everything before decisions are made. For homes in Tucson and the Catalina Foothills, we also think about how natural light, desert views, and open-concept layouts shape the way your kitchen connects to the rest of your home. What our planning process covers: ✔ 3D structural designs with room for revisions ✔ Custom kitchen cabinets planned around how you actually cook and gather ✔ Finish selections for counters, tile, lighting, and flooring ✔ A detailed budget you approve before construction begins Whether your project is a focused kitchen update or full interior remodeling that includes bathroom remodeling down the road, a thoughtful plan keeps everything cohesive and on track. Fall is a wonderful season to get started. Stop by our River Center design studio or send us a message to book your free consultation.

From the owner
Is your kitchen prepared for the Arizona climate? In Queen Creek, the intense sun and dry air can significantly impact the longevity of your kitchen materials. Selecting the right finishes is about more than just your aesthetic vision; it is about ensuring your investment stands up to our local environment. At NextGen Bath & Kitchen Remodeling, we help you navigate these practical challenges during the design phase. Common climate concerns: ☀️ Fading: Certain materials may lose their color vibrancy when exposed to indirect desert sunlight. 🌵 Warping: Low humidity can affect the stability of specific cabinetry and wood elements. 📉 Cracking: Rapid temperature shifts can impact certain countertop and flooring selections. Our team provides guidance on choosing durable materials that maintain their beauty and function over time. We focus on connecting your style with practical, long-lasting options for your home. Ready to get started? Schedule a free in-home consultation to review your options and begin your remodeling journey.

The client reached out with a request to update two full bathrooms and one half bathroom. According to the client, the bathrooms were around 30 years old! We were happy to complete this project for our client. In the master bathroom, we completed a full remodel. We completely built a new frame, replaced all plumbing, installed a classic shower pan liner waterproofing system, used RedGard for the walls, installed a glass shower door and quality faucets and fixtures. We also replaced the existing exhaust fan, light fixture, medicine cabinet, and vanity. The walls were also freshly painted. In the second bathroom, we completed a partial remodel. We kept the existing bathtub and replaced only the bathtub faucet. We removed the old glass shower door, installed new tile, a new medicine cabinet, light fixture, and vanity, and also painted the walls. WPS Remodeling opened up this exterior wall to replace rotted sheathing and framing behind the siding. From the outside, rot often shows up as soft trim, peeling paint that won't stay put, or siding that sits unevenly. Behind it, water that got past old flashing or a failing gutter can soak into the wood for years. The only lasting fix is to cut out the damaged wood back to solid material, replace the sheathing and any soft framing, add a weather barrier, and close it up with new siding and trim. Fall is the time to catch it: once freezing temperatures arrive, trapped moisture expands and the damage spreads. WPS Remodeling repairs rotted wood, trim, and siding, and replaces gutters, for homeowners in and around Westbrook, CT. Seeing soft or peeling trim on your house?
